_note: Curated content for the world physical, world history and drainage maps. 'ne' is the Natural Earth NAME used to find the shape. Pins are approximate city locations, for teaching.

physical.name: Himalayas
physical.why: Young fold mountains from the India–Eurasia collision; block cold Central Asian winds and force monsoon rain on the plains.

physical.name: Andes
physical.why: Fold mountains on the western edge of South America, where the Nazca Plate dives under the continent; part of the Ring of Fire.

physical.name: Rocky Mountains
physical.why: Western cordillera of North America, running north–south; they create a rain shadow over the Great Plains.

physical.name: Alps
physical.why: Fold mountains from the Africa–Eurasia collision; run east–west, so they shelter southern Europe from northern cold.

physical.name: Atlas Mountains
physical.why: Fold mountains of north-west Africa, also from the Africa–Eurasia collision.

physical.name: Zagros Mountains
physical.why: Fold belt where the Arabian Plate pushes into Eurasia; rich oil fields lie along its foothills.

physical.name: Ural Mountains
physical.why: Old, worn-down fold mountains in the interior of a continent; a rare exception to young ranges on continental edges.

physical.name: Appalachians
physical.why: Very old, eroded fold mountains on the eastern side of North America.

physical.name: Great Dividing Range
physical.why: Runs along eastern Australia; traps moisture from the Pacific trade winds, leaving the interior dry.

physical.name: Hindu Kush
physical.why: Range of Afghanistan and northern Pakistan; its passes were historic invasion and trade routes into India.

physical.name: Caucasus
physical.why: Range between the Black and Caspian seas; a corridor for pipelines and contested borders.

physical.name: Tian Shan
physical.why: Range of Central Asia; its glaciers feed rivers in a dry region.

physical.name: Sahara
physical.why: World's largest hot desert, on the western side of a continent around 20–30°N under subtropical high pressure.

physical.name: Arabian Desert (Rub' al Khali)
physical.why: Hot desert under the subtropical high; sits on huge oil and gas reserves.

physical.name: Thar Desert
physical.why: India's hot desert in the north-west; high solar potential and desertification risk.

physical.name: Sonoran Desert
physical.why: Hot desert on the western side of North America, around 30°N, dried further by the cold California current.

physical.name: Chihuahuan Desert
physical.why: Hot desert of northern Mexico, in the rain shadow of the Sierra Madre ranges.

physical.name: Atacama Desert
physical.why: One of the driest places on Earth: subtropical high pressure, the cold Peru (Humboldt) current and the Andes rain shadow.

physical.name: Namib Desert
physical.why: Coastal desert of south-west Africa, kept dry by the cold Benguela current.

physical.name: Kalahari
physical.why: Semi-arid basin of southern Africa, inland from the Namib.

physical.name: Great Victoria Desert
physical.why: Largest of Australia's deserts, in the dry western and central interior.

physical.name: Great Sandy Desert
physical.why: Hot desert of north-western Australia, around 20°S.

physical.name: Gobi
physical.why: Cold desert of Mongolia and China, dry because it is far inland and in the Himalayan–Tibetan rain shadow.

physical.name: Taklimakan
physical.why: Cold sandy desert in the Tarim Basin, ringed by high mountains.

physical.name: Tibetan Plateau
physical.why: Highest plateau on Earth; its summer heating helps drive the Indian monsoon and it feeds Asia's great rivers.

physical.name: Deccan Plateau
physical.why: Old, stable block of peninsular India; the Deccan traps give black cotton soil and mineral wealth.

physical.name: Brazilian Highlands
physical.why: Ancient plateau of eastern Brazil, rich in iron ore.

physical.name: Great Plains
physical.why: Temperate grassland of North America; a wheat and maize belt in the rain shadow of the Rockies.

physical.name: North European Plain
physical.why: Low, open plain across Europe; an easy route for armies in both World Wars.

physical.name: Pampas
physical.why: Fertile temperate grasslands of Argentina; wheat and cattle.

physical.name: Sahel
physical.why: Semi-arid belt south of the Sahara; a classic case of desertification.

physical.name: Amazon Basin
physical.why: Largest tropical rainforest; a global carbon sink under deforestation pressure.

physical.name: Congo Basin
physical.why: Second-largest tropical rainforest, astride the Equator.

seas.name: Bay of Bengal
seas.why: Warm, shallow waters and the funnel shape of its head make it a major cyclone basin.

seas.name: Arabian Sea
seas.why: Fewer cyclones than the Bay of Bengal, but warming waters are making them stronger.

seas.name: South China Sea
seas.why: Breeding ground for typhoons, and a contested sea under China's nine-dash line.

seas.name: Gulf of Mexico
seas.why: Warm waters feed Atlantic hurricanes; tornadoes are common inland where its moist air meets dry continental air.

seas.name: Persian Gulf
seas.why: Source of much of India's oil and gas imports; exits through the Strait of Hormuz.

seas.name: Red Sea
seas.why: Links the Suez Canal to the Indian Ocean through Bab-el-Mandeb.

seas.name: Mediterranean Sea
seas.why: Links the Suez route to Europe; site of many world history events.

rivers.name: Nile
rivers.why: Flows north through the Sahara; its waters are shared, and disputed, by Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia.

rivers.name: Amazon
rivers.why: Largest river by volume; drains the Amazon rainforest.

rivers.name: Congo
rivers.why: Crosses the Equator twice, so it carries water all year.

rivers.name: Mississippi
rivers.why: Drains the Great Plains into the Gulf of Mexico; a key inland waterway.

rivers.name: Yangtze
rivers.why: China's longest river; the Three Gorges Dam shows the trade-offs of big dams.

rivers.name: Mekong
rivers.why: Rises in Tibet and flows through six countries; upstream dams in China worry the lower Mekong states.

rivers.name: Danube
rivers.why: Flows through ten countries into the Black Sea; an international waterway.

rivers.name: Ob
rivers.why: Siberian river flowing north into the Arctic Ocean; frozen for much of the year.

history_pins.name: Boston
history_pins.event: Boston Tea Party (1773): colonists protest British taxes and the trade monopoly.

history_pins.name: Philadelphia
history_pins.event: Declaration of Independence (1776) adopted by the American colonies.

history_pins.name: Paris
history_pins.event: Storming of the Bastille (1789) begins the French Revolution.

history_pins.name: Manchester
history_pins.event: Centre of the cotton-textile factories of Britain's Industrial Revolution.

history_pins.name: Tokyo
history_pins.event: Meiji Restoration (1868): the state drives Japan's rapid 'latecomer' industrialisation.

history_pins.name: Berlin
history_pins.event: Berlin Conference (1884–85): European powers set rules for dividing Africa.

history_pins.name: Sarajevo
history_pins.event: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand (1914) triggers the First World War.

history_pins.name: Petrograd (St Petersburg)
history_pins.event: Russian Revolution (1917); Lenin's New Economic Policy follows in 1921.

history_pins.name: Versailles
history_pins.event: Treaty of Versailles (1919) ends the First World War on harsh terms for Germany.

history_pins.name: New York
history_pins.event: Wall Street Crash (1929) begins the Great Depression.

history_pins.name: Hiroshima
history_pins.event: Atomic bombing (1945) ends the Second World War in Asia.

history_pins.name: Suez
history_pins.event: Suez Crisis (1956): Egypt nationalises the canal; the failed Anglo-French invasion ends Britain's great-power image.

history_pins.name: Accra
history_pins.event: Ghana (Gold Coast) becomes independent in 1957, the first in sub-Saharan Africa, under Kwame Nkrumah.

history_pins.name: Kuala Lumpur
history_pins.event: Malaya becomes independent in 1957 after the Malayan Emergency; ethnic balance shapes the new state.
